moves.name: Body Feint Left
moves.description: Shift your body weight sharply to the left to wrong-foot the defender. One of the most fundamental moves in football — master this before anything else.
tips: Combine immediately with a burst of sprint in the opposite direction
Works best when defender is standing still or moving toward you
Don't overuse — defenders adapt quickly to repeated feints
Effective near the touchline to create crossing space

moves.name: Body Feint Right
moves.description: Mirror of the Body Feint Left. Lean right to pull the defender, then burst left or straight ahead.
tips: Pair with a quick left sprint after for maximum effect
Use in tight midfield areas to create passing lanes
The timing of the flick defines how convincing the feint looks
Practice alternating left/right feints rhythmically

moves.name: Stepover (Right)
moves.description: Step over the ball from right to left. A classic dribbling trick that can be chained for devastating effect against committed defenders.
tips: The RS arc goes from down-right to right — think of drawing a 'C'
Chain 2–3 stepovers to keep the defender guessing
Slow down slightly before the stepover so the fake lands effectively
Combine with a sprint burst afterward to exploit the created gap

inputs.label: Rotate RS from Down-Right to Right (CW arc)

moves.name: Stepover (Left)
moves.description: Step over the ball from left to right. Mirror of the right stepover. Essential for ambidextrous dribbling.
tips: RS arc goes from down-left to left — mirror of the right stepover
Practice switching between left and right stepovers
Works well on the right flank when cutting inside
Add pace variation: slow approach, explosive exit

inputs.label: Rotate RS from Down-Left to Left (CCW arc)

moves.name: Heel-to-Heel Flick
moves.description: Flick the ball forward with one heel, then knock it back with the other. A rapid two-touch move that creates uncertainty in the defender.
tips: Both flicks must be fast — less than half a beat between them
The forward flick direction matches your run direction
Use when stationary or slow-dribbling — speed kills the effect
Great when a defender is right behind you tracking your movement

moves.name: Ball Roll (Right)
moves.description: Roll the ball sideways to the right while shielding with your body. Creates space to shift direction or find a passing lane.
tips: Hold L2 firmly throughout — releasing early cancels the move
The ball roll speed depends on your player's dribbling stats
Chain with a fake shot to send defenders the wrong way
Use from a standing position for the cleanest execution

moves.name: Ball Roll (Left)
moves.description: Roll the ball to the left while using your body to shield. The left variation — equally important to practice both sides.
tips: Same mechanics as Ball Roll Right but mirrored
Practice transitioning from Ball Roll Right directly into Ball Roll Left
Your player's weak foot rating does NOT affect ball rolls
Use facing a corner flag to roll away from defenders approaching from behind

moves.name: Drag Back
moves.description: Pull the ball backward sharply, reversing direction to escape pressure. A fundamental possession skill — used by top players every match.
tips: Hold L2 before inputting LS down — the order matters
Follow immediately with a new run direction on LS after the drag
Most effective when a defender commits to a tackle
Combine with a body feint before the drag to confuse the AI

inputs.label: Hold L2 + Push LS Down (toward your player)

moves.name: Fake Shot
moves.description: Shape as if to shoot or pass, then cancel — sending the goalkeeper and defenders diving the wrong way. One of the most versatile moves in football.
tips: The LS direction at cancellation is the actual exit direction
Use near the box — the threat of a shot makes this lethal
Works as a fake pass too: tap △ then quickly ✕
Slow down before input for a convincing wind-up animation

inputs.label: Quickly tap ✕ (cancel) + move LS in exit direction

moves.name: Roulette (Right)
moves.description: A 360° spin move turning the player right while shielding the ball. Based on the Zidane/Maradona roulette — protects the ball throughout the rotation.
tips: Hold L2 for the entire duration of the rotation
RS rotation is clockwise — start from the top (up) and sweep right
Player direction affects the spin — face the right way before executing
Most effective with high-agility players (90+ agility)

moves.name: Roulette (Left)
moves.description: The counter-clockwise spin variation. Turning left — important to master both directions for maximum unpredictability.
tips: Counter-clockwise: start RS up, sweep left then down
The dominant direction of your player's run affects exit direction
Chain with a burst sprint immediately after completing the rotation
Advanced: vary speed of rotation to delay or accelerate exit

moves.name: Heel Chop (Right)
moves.description: A sharp heel chop that cuts the ball to the right while sprinting. Explosive direction change — great for beating a defender in a footrace.
tips: Input while sprinting (holding R2) for maximum speed burst after
The cut direction changes based on your run direction
Works best in open space with room to accelerate after the chop
Pair with L2 Ball Roll before the chop to feint then cut

inputs.label: Hold L2 + Flick RS Right (sharp chop)

moves.name: Heel Chop (Left)
moves.description: Heel chop to the left — the mirror variation. Equally dangerous when cutting inside from the right flank.
tips: Mirror of Heel Chop Right — the left version is slightly harder for most players
Great for right-footed wingers on the right side cutting inside
Sprint beforehand — the chop changes momentum dramatically
Time it just as the defender lunges to maximize the separation

inputs.label: Hold L2 + Flick RS Left (sharp chop)

moves.name: Scoop Turn (Right)
moves.description: Scoop the ball to the right in a tight turning motion. Quick and deceptive — effective in crowded midfield areas.
tips: RS flick right while stationary produces the cleanest scoop
Different from a ball roll — this has more of a scooping arc motion
Works especially well in the final third to create a shot angle
Combine with a stepover beforehand to compound the defender's confusion

moves.name: Elastico (Right)
moves.description: Ronaldinho's signature move. Flick the ball to the outside foot, then whip it back past the defender in one fluid motion. One of the most iconic skill moves in football.
tips: Both RS flicks must happen rapidly — there is no pause between them
The first flick goes to the outside foot (right); the second cuts back hard left
Practice the two-flick rhythm at slow BPM first, then build up
Player must have 4★+ skill rating to execute this move
The return flick angle should be ±15° — precision matters here

moves.name: Reverse Elastico (Right)
moves.description: The inverse of the Elastico — fake to the inside first, then snap to the outside. Less common than the original, which makes it harder to read.
tips: Flick RS LEFT first (inside fake), then snap RIGHT — opposite of regular Elastico
The surprise element is higher than the regular Elastico at top level
Chain directly after a regular Elastico for a devastating double fake
Equally fast rhythm required — don't slow between the two flicks

moves.name: Advanced Rainbow Flick
moves.description: Chip the ball over the defender's head in a looping arc. The advanced version includes a final directional flick to guide where the ball lands.
tips: Three-part move: RS down → RS down again → RS up
The first two RS inputs are slower; the final up flick is sharp
Use when a defender commits to a slide tackle — the ball sails over them
High agility and ball control players execute this most effectively
Practice the rhythm: slow-slow-FAST

inputs.label: Flick RS Up (sharp — launch the ball)

moves.name: Sombrero Flick (Forward)
moves.description: Lift the ball over the defender with a sombrero touch while using L1 for finesse control. Flick forward to launch it ahead of you.
tips: Hold L1 throughout — this is the skill modifier for the sombrero
RS flick forward (up) while L1 held lifts the ball over the defender's head
Requires the player to be stationary or slow-dribbling
Follow with a sprint to collect the ball ahead of the outrun defender

moves.name: Sombrero Flick (Backward)
moves.description: Lift the ball backward over a chasing defender. Useful for reversing direction while keeping the ball in the air.
tips: Hold L1 + flick RS down — opposite of the forward sombrero
Most useful when a defender is directly behind you applying pressure
The ball travels backward — ensure you have the awareness to collect
Chain with a 180° turn sprint to run onto the airborne ball

moves.name: Ball Roll Fake Turn
moves.description: Begin a ball roll, then abruptly reverse direction — the defender follows the fake roll, and you exit the other way.
tips: Start a ball roll right, then immediately flick RS left (or vice versa)
The fake must be convincing — let the first roll begin before reversing
Gap between roll and reverse: half a beat maximum
Devastating in 1v1 situations near the penalty area

inputs.label: Hold L2 + Flick RS Right (fake roll)
Hold L2 + Flick RS Left (reverse — fast!)

moves.name: Berba Spin
moves.description: Named after Dimitar Berbatov. A subtle, controlled spin while shielding the ball — creates separation in tight areas without committing to a full rotation.
tips: Hold L2 + flick RS diagonally (down-right or down-left depending on direction)
Less flashy than the Roulette but harder to tackle
Perfect for strikers with their back to goal — spin into shooting position
Requires precise diagonal RS input — practice the exact angle

inputs.label: Hold L2 + Flick RS Down-Right (precise diagonal)

moves.name: La Croqueta (Left)
moves.description: Iniesta's masterpiece. Using the sole of the foot, drag the ball from right to left in a quick, deceptive touch. Executed with L1 + RS flick left — the signature of elite dribblers.
tips: Speed is everything — L1 must be held, then RS flick left immediately
The move shifts the ball to your left foot while creating a small window to shoot or pass
Most effective when the defender commits to your right side
5-star skill players execute the smoothest animation — it matters
Slow BPM practice first: nail the L1 + RS timing before speeding up

moves.name: La Croqueta (Right)
moves.description: La Croqueta in the right direction. Drag the ball from left to right with sole touch. Equally effective — master both directions for complete unpredictability.
tips: L1 held + RS flick right — same rhythm as the left version
The double croqueta (left then right or vice versa) is an advanced combo
Aim to execute in under 300ms for the most effective in-game result
Can be used as a fake shot setup: croqueta right, then shoot left

moves.name: Rainbow Flick
moves.description: The ultimate showboat move. Flick the ball up over your own head and the defender in a rainbow arc. Three-beat RS input — one of the most difficult skill moves to time correctly.
tips: Three flicks: RS down (slow), RS down again (medium), RS up (FAST)
The rhythm is NOT even — slow, slightly faster, then snap up hard
The final upward flick must cross the FLICK_THRESHOLD in under 80ms
Only attempt with players who have 5★ skill moves
Use when a defender is directly in front pressing — the ball sails over them
Master at 70 BPM before attempting at 100+ BPM

inputs.label: Flick RS Up — SNAP it hard and fast

moves.name: Hocus Pocus
moves.description: A deceptive two-part rotation that makes the ball appear to go one way, then suddenly shifts the other. Requires precise RS rotation control and is one of the hardest 5-star moves to master.
tips: Two clockwise rotations in quick succession — RS → CW → neutral → CW
The brief neutral between rotations is critical — don't make it continuous
Very hard to read at game speed — high 5-star skill players only
Practice the individual rotations first, then combine
At 90 BPM this move requires near-perfect timing — start at 60 BPM

inputs.label: Brief neutral — flick RS to UP (reset position)

moves.name: Triple Elastico
moves.description: Three consecutive Elasticos in rapid succession. Devastates defenders who start tracking after the first fake — the third snaps them the wrong way completely.
tips: Three pairs of RS right→left flicks with minimal gap between pairs
The tempo must be consistent — all three pairs at the same rhythm
The key is keeping the RS snaps sharp and returning to neutral between pairs
Slow this down to 60 BPM to learn the rhythm, then build to 110+
Only attempt in 1v1 situations — too slow for group defenders

moves.name: Ball Roll to Chop
moves.description: Begin a ball roll, then snap into a sharp chop in the perpendicular direction. A two-phase move that changes direction twice — extremely difficult to defend against.
tips: L2 held throughout, RS right for the roll, then RS down for the chop cut
The LS direction after the chop determines your final exit direction
Timing between roll and chop: one beat max — faster = more unpredictable
This is a 5-star move — lesser skilled players execute it slower and less convincingly
Master Ball Roll and Heel Chop separately before combining

inputs.label: Hold L2 + Flick RS Right (start roll)
Hold L2 + Flick RS Down (chop cut — fast!)

sequences.name: Double Elastico Fake
sequences.description: Chain a regular Elastico immediately into a Reverse Elastico. The two-direction fake is nearly impossible to read at game speed.

moves.timingNote: Execute cleanly — the snap must be sharp
Immediately after — no pause. The defender commits on the first fake.

sequences.name: Stepover Chain (3x)
sequences.description: Three consecutive stepovers right, building rhythm and selling the direction change more convincingly each time.

moves.timingNote: First stepover — sets up the expectation
Second — defender starts tracking
Third — commit to the burst now

sequences.name: Ball Roll into Fake Shot
sequences.description: Start a ball roll to create lateral movement, then cancel into a fake shot. The defender reacts to the roll direction, the goalkeeper dives to the fake shot — you have a clear lane.

moves.timingNote: Roll right to pull the defender
Fake shot toward the vacated space on the left

sequences.name: Double La Croqueta
sequences.description: La Croqueta left immediately into La Croqueta right. Two rapid sole-of-foot touches create a zig-zag that no defender can track.

moves.timingNote: Snap left with precision
Immediately right — zero gap. L1 stays held.

sequences.name: Roulette into Sprint
sequences.description: Execute a full roulette spin then immediately release L2 and burst forward. The spin buys time and space; the sprint capitalizes on it.

moves.timingNote: Full 270° CW rotation
Release L2, feint once, then hold R2 to sprint

sequences.name: Heel-to-Heel into Elastico
sequences.description: Use the Heel-to-Heel Flick to get the defender moving forward, then snap an Elastico as they close the gap.

moves.timingNote: Quick forward-back flick to bait the defender
As they lunge — execute the Elastico

sequences.name: Berba Spin into La Croqueta
sequences.description: The Berba Spin creates confusion about the exit direction. Immediately follow with La Croqueta to fully commit the defender the wrong way before breaking.

moves.timingNote: The spin is the setup — sell it with your LS direction
Croqueta fires before the defender recovers from tracking the spin

sequences.name: Rainbow Flick Setup Sequence
sequences.description: Slow the game with a drag back, reset with a ball roll, then launch the Rainbow Flick when the defender steps in.

moves.timingNote: Reset the play — drag back to create separation
Roll right to position the ball
As defender commits to the roll direction — launch the Rainbow

sequences.name: Five-Star Showcase
sequences.description: A showcase sequence combining three elite 5-star moves: La Croqueta, Hocus Pocus, and the Rainbow Flick. The ultimate skill display.

moves.timingNote: Open with the Croqueta — shift left
While they adjust — execute Hocus Pocus
Final exclamation mark — Rainbow over the committed defender

sequences.name: Close Control Escape
sequences.description: Three moves chained to escape from tight defensive pressure: drag back to reset, heel chop to change direction, then burst with a body feint.

moves.timingNote: Pull away from the initial pressure
Change direction sharply
Final feint to open the run channel

drills.name: Fundamentals Warm-Up
drills.description: Start every session with this. Cycle through basic feints and stepovers to warm up your thumbs and calibrate muscle memory.

drills.name: Ball Roll Mastery
drills.description: Perfect the L2 + RS timing for all ball roll variants. Focus on holding L2 cleanly and flicking the RS with precision.

drills.name: Elastico Builder
drills.description: Build up to the full Elastico from its components. Start with single flicks, then master the rapid two-flick combo.

drills.name: L1 Modifier Moves
drills.description: Build the L1 hold reflex. Every move here requires L1 held — train your left index finger to hold without affecting the LS.

drills.name: Five-Star Gauntlet
drills.description: The hardest drill. All 5-star moves in sequence at competitive BPM. If you can complete this with 80% accuracy, you are match-ready.
